title: [kafka] increase on memory after upgrade clickhouse from version 23.1 to version 23.8.1.2992
body: After upgrading ClickHouse from version 23.1 to 23.8.1.2992, I observed a significant increase in memory usage. The same queries that used about 500 MB on the older version are now recorded as using about 2.27 GB. Is there a recommended solution, or should I revert to the previous version?

symptoms_visible: After upgrading from ClickHouse 23.1 to 23.8.1.2992, queries previously recorded at about 500 MB are recorded at up to about 2.27 GB.
N0.label: N0 memory increase reported after upgrade

symptoms_visible: The query-log entries for my wide filtered query are around 1.8–2.1 GB after the upgrade, compared with roughly 450–485 MB before it.
N1.label: N1 query workload characterized

symptoms_visible: MemoryResident reaches 27366715392 bytes and rises over time, while restarting ClickHouse releases the accumulated memory.
A query recorded around 2 GB in system.query_log uses only about 200 MB when I copy and run it manually.
N2.label: N2 process RSS growth established

symptoms_visible: After upgrading to 23.8.2.7, the process memory still increases and is released by restarting ClickHouse.
N2_x.label: N2_x upgrade attempt aftermath

symptoms_visible: The process memory continues rising on an affected setup even when client queries are disabled and only Kafka ingestion through materialized views remains active.
N3.label: N3 growth narrowed to Kafka ingestion activity

symptoms_visible: After my first attempt to apply the suggested Kafka configuration setting, the process memory still continued to rise.
N4.label: N4 first configuration probe inconclusive

symptoms_visible: After placing statistics_interval_ms=0 inside the kafka configuration group and restarting ClickHouse, MemoryResident remained stable for the next 16 hours.
N_terminal.label: terminal Kafka statistics disabled and RSS stable

question_patterns: Can you provide a reproducible table definition and the query whose memory usage increased?
Please share a representative schema and select query.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The table has about 40 columns and uses ReplicatedMergeTree, partitioned by day and ordered by (col_1, col_2). The query selects about 29 columns, filters col_1 with an IN list and the last 60 days, applies several numeric filters, and uses LIMIT 10000 BY col_1.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The increase occurs with an empty MergeTree table and a simple SELECT 1, without any Kafka ingestion.

question_patterns: What is the type of the time column used in toYYYYMMDD?
Did you mean LIMIT 10000 BY col_1?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes, I mean LIMIT 10000 BY col_1.

question_patterns: How many items are normally in the IN list?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: It can contain 1 or 500 values, depending on the query.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: It normally contains between 10 and 450 values.

edges.comment: Reporter messages c2, c4 and c8: the opening reporter supplied the schema, representative query, DateTime type, corrected LIMIT BY syntax, and IN-list cardinality.

question_patterns: Instead of MemoryTracking, what value does MemoryResident show in system.asynchronous_metrics?
Can you measure the server process RSS using the MemoryResident asynchronous metric?

counterfactual_candidates.answer: MemoryResident remains flat near 1 GB while only MemoryTracking rises.
MemoryResident is about 26 GB rather than 27366715392 bytes exactly.

question_patterns: Does the same query consume around 2 GB when you execute it manually?
Can you compare a high-memory query-log entry with a manual execution of the same SQL and values?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I copied the same query and values from a query_log entry recorded around 2 GB, but when I ran it manually its memory usage was only around 200 MB.

question_patterns: Do your SELECT queries use Distributed tables, or how are the shards queried?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I query each shard individually and do not read from the replicas.

edges.comment: Reporter messages c8, c14, c15, c18, c20, c22 and c24: the reporter measured process RSS, explained that restarts release it, compared query_log with a manual run, and described direct shard access. The statement that ingestion and processing did not change was volunteered in c14.

solution.intent: Treat the issue as already corrected in the next 23.8 maintenance build and upgrade to 23.8.2.7.
solution.concrete_example: Upgrade the affected server to ClickHouse 23.8.2.7 and monitor MemoryResident.

edges.comment: Maintainer suggestion c25 and reporter result c28: the reporter upgraded to 23.8.2.7, but the increasing process memory remained. The separate prewhere configuration suggestion was not clearly confirmed as applied and is therefore not encoded as falsified.

question_patterns: What continuous background activity remains on the affected cluster?
Are you using a message-queue table engine for ingestion?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I am also using the Kafka engine.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Kafka is not configured anywhere on my cluster; all ingestion is through synchronous INSERT statements.

question_patterns: If client queries are disabled and only ingestion remains, does the process memory still rise?
Can you isolate whether the growth continues with only the ingestion pipeline active?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: On an affected setup, we disabled client queries and everything else we could, leaving only Kafka consumption and materialized views writing MergeTree tables. The process memory still increased.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: With client queries disabled and Kafka ingestion left running, MemoryResident stays flat; it rises only while the dashboard SELECT runs.
The same growth occurs with two Kafka consumers instead of one while client queries remain disabled.

edges.comment: Reporter c33 states that the opening reporter also uses Kafka. The isolation result comes from participant3's affected Kafka deployment in c31 and is explicitly folded into the simulated user side as corroborating evidence; it is not represented as a test performed on the reporter's own cluster.

question_patterns: Please apply the configuration toggle just suggested, restart if required, and report what happens to MemoryResident.
After trying the proposed Kafka configuration change, does the process RSS stop increasing?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I applied the setting as I understood the instructions, but the issue still persisted.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: After the first configuration attempt and restart, MemoryResident remained stable for several days.

edges.comment: Maintainer suggestion c41-c44 and reporter response c45: this was a handler-initiated configuration-toggle probe. The reporter reported only that the first application did not change the observation; the later successful nested configuration shows that this result did not falsify the underlying Kafka-statistics diagnosis.

solution.intent: Disable Kafka statistics collection with the setting correctly nested inside the server's kafka configuration group, restart ClickHouse, and monitor process RSS before declaring the issue resolved.
solution.concrete_example: Create a config.d/kafka.xml file containing <yandex><kafka><statistics_interval_ms>0</statistics_interval_ms></kafka></yandex>, restart ClickHouse, and monitor system.asynchronous_metrics MemoryResident. The reporter observed stable memory for 16 hours after applying this form.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter supplied the raw isolation and configuration outcomes. Connecting the successful correctly nested toggle to Kafka statistics collection as the cause is the maintainer-side diagnosis supported by the linked fixes and the reporter's post-restart observation.

edges.comment: Resolution chain c41-c46, c54 and c59-c61: maintainers suspected the Kafka statistics functionality; the initial application did not work, but the reporter later created config.d/kafka.xml with statistics_interval_ms nested under kafka, restarted, and observed stable memory for 16 hours. The linked pull requests are factual records but are not scored because their identifiers and implementation details were not introduced by the reporter before resolution.

solution.intent: Disable Kafka statistics collection with the setting correctly nested inside the kafka server configuration, restart ClickHouse, and verify that process RSS remains stable.
solution.concrete_example: Add <kafka><statistics_interval_ms>0</statistics_interval_ms></kafka> under the server configuration root in config.d/kafka.xml, restart ClickHouse, and monitor MemoryResident over time.
solution.inference_hint: This shortcut permits an agent that recognizes the Kafka statistics regression from the opening Kafka context to propose the accepted configuration immediately, while still requiring post-restart RSS verification.

edges.comment: Shortcut copy of the accepted resolution, required because the canonical thread passed through the falsified maintenance-upgrade attempt before reaching the Kafka statistics diagnosis.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted cause as Kafka statistics collection on the affected ClickHouse deployment, grounded in the Kafka-only ingestion evidence and the successful configuration probe rather than attributing the growth to the representative SELECT alone.
Must configure statistics_interval_ms to 0 inside the kafka configuration group, restart ClickHouse, and monitor the process-level MemoryResident metric.
Must not present upgrading to another 23.8 maintenance build as sufficient; the reporter confirmed that the memory growth remained after that upgrade.
Must distinguish process RSS growth from an individual query's query_log memory_usage and must not rely on MemoryTracking alone.
Must ask the affected user to verify that MemoryResident remains stable after restart before declaring the issue resolved; the graph surfaces the reporter's 16-hour stable observation.

persona_hint.experience_level: Operationally experienced ClickHouse administrator who can run system-table diagnostics, edit server configuration files, restart nodes, and compare cluster metrics, but needs guidance on unfamiliar settings and memory diagnostics.
persona_hint.communication_style: Cooperative and persistent; supplies SQL, measurements, and configuration results in detail, asks for exact configuration instructions, and reports practical production observations over time.
